stem: $P$ is a point with co-ordinates $({=x}, {=y})$ on a Cartesian plane, and $O$ is the origin. $OP$ forms an angle, $\theta$, measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis. Without using a calculator, which of the following is $\sec\theta$?
solution: Read off the co-ordinates of $P$ and keep their signs: $x={=x}$ and $y={=y}$. The point lies in quadrant {=q}.

We find $r=OP$ with the theorem of Pythagoras. $r$ is a length, so it is positive in every quadrant: $\begin{aligned}r^{2}&=x^{2}+y^{2}\\&=({=x})^{2}+({=y})^{2}\\&={=r2}\\r&=\sqrt{{=r2}}\end{aligned}$
$\sec\theta$ is the reciprocal of $\cos\theta=\frac{x}{r}$, so it is $r$ over $x$ (not $r$ over $y$): $\begin{aligned}\sec\theta&=\frac{r}{x}\\&=\frac{\sqrt{{=r2}}}{{=x}}\end{aligned}$

proposed_misconceptions.label: Gives the ratio itself instead of its reciprocal
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student finds x over r correctly but writes it as sec, the value of cos, instead of turning the fraction over to get r over x.

notes: Standard tier, a choice question because every distractor is one named slip. Correct: r/x. D1 pairs sec with y (catalogued mc reciprocal-named-by-letters: sec taken as r over y). D2 gives r a negative sign (catalogued mc r-takes-sign-of-point); the point is kept out of quadrant I so that this slip changes the value. D3 is cos (x over r), a new misconception declared here. Constraints keep all four options distinct in value: |x| != |y| (so r/y is neither r/x nor -r/x), r2 neither a square nor divisible by a square. |x| >= 2 avoids a denominator of 1 or -1 in the key. The stem carries the coordinates, so no distinct_by_choices is needed. Instances: 129 distinct points.
